findings.text: In the already-installed branch, the default-packages and reinstall-packages guards are inverted to `[ $EXIT_CODE -ne 0 ]`. `EXIT_CODE` is also declared `local` but never initialised. With `nvm install <v>` on an installed version and no npm upgrade, `EXIT_CODE` is empty, so the test errors and evaluates false. Default packages and `--reinstall-packages-from` are silently skipped. They would run only after a previous step had failed.

The alias step is guarded by `[ $EXIT_CODE -ne 0 ] && [ -n "${ALIAS-}" ]`, which is inverted. `nvm install --alias=foo <installed version>` never creates the alias when the earlier steps succeeded or `EXIT_CODE` is unset. If `nvm use` failed, `EXIT_CODE` is unset and `return $EXIT_CODE` returns an empty or unrelated status.

`nvm_install_default_packages` assigns `EXIT_CODE` without declaring it `local`, so it overwrites the caller's or global `EXIT_CODE`. It also moves the default-packages file read to after installation. A failure reading the file used to abort before installing anything. Now the node version is already installed when the error is returned.

2.reason: The unscoped EXIT_CODE does change the caller's local EXIT_CODE, but every call site sets EXIT_CODE=$? straight after the call, so the change has no effect; and reading default-packages after installing is a deliberate refactor, since the read moved into nvm_install_default_packages and a read error is still returned as the exit code.
